caption: Where empty lots can be created is constrained by the surrounding tiles.
content: Creating an empty lot strongly constrains which tiles can be placed around it. As a result, there are fewer places where empty lots can be created than you might expect.

Unless there is a tile that can fill a cell like @m{unsatisfied}, @b{you cannot create an empty lot that occupies a 3 × 3 area}. In other words, @b{the vertical or horizontal width of an empty lot must always be exactly two cells}. Keeping this in mind makes it easier to narrow down the possible shapes of empty lots.

content.caption: Example
content: Assuming the tiles in your inventory are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} @t{forest_open.1.dr} @t{forest_open.2s.r} @t{forest_open_road.r} and their rotations, let's solve the Area below.
First, if we focus on the cell @m{pending}, the tiles that can be placed there are either @t{forest_road.2t.dl} or @t{forest_open.1.dl}.
If you place @t{forest_open.1.dl} on the cell @m{pending}, the only tile that can be placed in the cell to the left is @t{forest_open_road.u}.
As a result, the empty lot must take the following shape, with a height of two cells, leaving no tile that can be placed on the cell @m{unsatisfied}.
Therefore, we can conclude that the tile to place on the cell @m{pending} must be @t{forest_road.2t.dl}, not @t{forest_open.1.dl}.

Next, if we focus on the cell @m{pending}, the same technique can be applied. If you place @t{forest_open.1.ur}, the empty lot can only take the following shape in order not to conflict with the road tile @t{forest_road.2t.dl} above. In this case as well, there will be no tile that can be placed on the cell @m{unsatisfied}.
Therefore, the tile to place on the cell @m{pending} must be @t{forest_road.2t.ur}.

Next, if we focus on the cell @m{pending}, @t{forest_open.1.dl} cannot be placed here. If you place @t{forest_open.1.dl}, the empty lot will take the following shape, making it impossible to fill the remaining cells.
Therefore, the tile to place on the cell @m{pending} must be @t{forest_road.2t.dl}, and the surrounding road tiles are determined as follows.
Finally, create a road dead end in the remaining space to complete the Area.
